summary: Kogen Mizuno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned a Doctorate of Letters from the University of Tokyo in 1928, later serving as professor there (1959–1962) and as professor and president (1976) at Komazawa University.

Specializing in Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Kogi Kudara served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1979, 1997) and was affiliated with the Ryukoku Buddhist Society as an editor (attested 2002).

Koichi Hokazono works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD at Kyushu University, later holding posts at Kyushu University (attested 1995) and The International University of Kagoshima as professor (attested 1991–2000).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, Koichi Shinohara served as a professor at McMaster University (~1974–2004) and as a Senior Lecturer in Religious Studies at Yale University (~2004–2021).

Koichi Takahashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under supervisors Ekyo Ejima and Akira Saito, subsequently serving there as an assistant (attested 2005) and project researcher (attested 2015).

Koichi Yokoyama specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his graduate studies at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and traditional teacher Gyōin Hashimoto, and served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1974–2006).
Koin Takada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1941–1944). A disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto, he succeeded him in 1967.

Koji Kamioka was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and under Yutaka Ochihara, later lecturing at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and serving as assistant professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

Koji Takahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Bukkyo University, earning a doctorate from the latter by 1991. He served at Bukkyo University as assistant professor (~1966–2005) and professor (~1975–2005).

Kojiro Yoshikawa was a Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1923–1926). He served as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Kyoto University (~1947–1967) and as board chairman of Toho Gakkai (~1975–1980).

Kojun Fukui worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a doctorate at Waseda University under Sokichi Tsuda and became professor there (1941–1969), while also serving as president of Taisho University (1928–1968, 1972–1975).
Kojun Saito was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University from ~1950 to ~1960. He held posts at Rissho University as assistant professor (~1970–1978) and department head (~1978–2002).
Kokyo Kawagishi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and International Buddhist University (attested 1976).
Konchok Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Dilgo Khyentse.
Konchok Gyatso is a Tibetologist who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Konchok Zangpo was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Konrad Klaus specializes in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn, served as interim professor at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn (1999–2001), and succeeded Claus Vogel in 2001.
Kosaku Hamada was an archaeology and Sinology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905). He held a post at the University of Tokyo and served at Kyoto University (~1909–1938).
